text:
maria: Quick heads-up — planning to flip the new routing policy default in the SDKs next week. Console doesn't surface per-route quota heatmaps yet, and telemetry mapping is incomplete. I'd like to gate the rollout until we have reliable signals.

aj: +1 we need per-route token burn, request error rate, and observed routing fallback counts. Current sampling drops route headers ~30% due to the proxy rewrite.

leo: Can we do a soft canary in the console? e.g. a feature flag that enables default routing for 10% of orgs and shows a dedicated tile with route-level metrics.

maria: Exactly. The canary tile should show: tokens/sec by route, quota burn %, p99 latency, and fallback rate to compatible models.

sdk-oliver: Heads-up — python SDK v1.4.0 renames header `X-Redwood-Route` -> `X-Redwood-Route-Hint` to avoid collisions. We can add a compatibility shim but it requires a minor release.

sre-sarah: If we add a shim server-side we avoid forcing customers to upgrade immediately. But the shim must be visible in telemetry (so we can measure how many requests relied on fallback). Add metric `redwood.route_header_fallback_count`.

aj: I'll add an opt-in sampling flag in the edge proxy to preserve full route headers at 100% for canary orgs, and leave global sampling at current levels otherwise. Config will be: `sampling.route_headers_canary = true` per-tenant.

leo: UI wiring: I can add a console tile that queries the new `/internal/route-metrics` endpoint (needs RBAC). We should return: { "route": "string", "tokens": number, "quota_pct": number, "fallbacks": number } — lightweight.

product-anna: Support and docs note: we need a short migration guide for SDK users (what to expect when header name is different + timeline). Also add a small blurb in release notes about the canary opt-in.

maria: Action list (short):
- aj: implement per-tenant sampling opt-in and expose sampling flag in the console (owner: aj)
- sdk-oliver: implement header fallback in Python + short-lived deprecation warning (owner: oliver)
- leo: console tile + storyboard for canary UX (owner: leo)
- sre-sarah: add `route_header_fallback_count` + link to grafana (owner: sara)
- product-anna: migration doc + release blurb (owner: anna)

sdk-oliver: For fallback impl I'll add server parsing like: `route = req.headers.get('X-Redwood-Route-Hint') or req.headers.get('X-Redwood-Route')` and log a warning on first use per session. Plan to ship in a patch before the canary.

aj: Example smoke test curl: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Route: user-chat" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — confirm tile shows `route=user-chat`.

sre-sarah: Also ensure throttling math accounts for fallback cases. If fallback triggers extra model calls, we must surface that on the tile as `extra_tokens_from_fallback`.

leo: UX question: show canary as a toggle per-org or per-project? I'd prefer per-org to minimize rollout complexity.

maria: Per-org is fine for initial canary. We'll later add per-project if needed.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: `edge-proxy@canary-sampling` -> staging (hash: a1b2c3).

aj: I'll push the canary proxy config to staging today and enable sampling for our test org `redwood-canary-org`.

sre-sarah: I'll create the grafana panel and add an alert: when fallback_rate > 2% and p95 latency increase > 50ms for 10m -> page on-call.

product-anna: Timeline check: feature freeze Wed EOD, staged canary Thu morning, monitor Thu-Fri, decide to expand Mon. Is that doable? :calendar: 

maria: Yes — tentative timeline looks good. If anyone needs more runway speak up now.

leo: I'll sketch the tile mock by EOD.

sdk-oliver: I'll open the Python PR with fallback + tests in the next 6 hours and add a note to changelog.

aj: I'll share config PR and small smoke test script in this thread when ready.

sre-sarah: I'll post the grafana link once panels are live.

maria: Thanks all. Let's keep this thread for the rollout checklist and small updates only. :thumbsup:
